text:
maya: Quick follow-up to the Access Router RFC — proposing a refactor that moves RBAC evaluation upstream from the query fanout.

maya: TL;DR: split responsibilities: Access Router decides route & visibility, Query Broker focuses on data retrieval and caching. This should reduce cache key entropy and let us keep low p50 for dashboard reads.

alex: I like the idea. What's the plan for tenant-scoped views? we can't duplicate logic per consumer.

pranav: core tradeoff: duplication vs coupling. If Router emits a visibility mask + route token, Broker can cache by (route_token, query_hash) instead of full user perms.

sara: can we get an example of the token shape? worried about token churn causing cache misses.

maya: example:
```
{ "route_token": "r:dash_v2:org:123:proj:5:view:summary", "visibility_mask": ["row:team:42","col:cost"], "ttl": 30 }
```
Broker uses route_token as primary cache key, visibility_mask applied at render time.

alex: hmm TTL 30s seems low for dashboards. If route changes (new perms) we need immediate revocation.

pranav: we can support revocation by bumping a per-org version in the token. Router increments on policy change; Broker invalidates when version mismatches.

julian: metrics we need: cache hit rate by route_token, p50/p95 dashboard load, error rate when visibility_mask rejects rows. Also track token churn.

sara: operationally, how does this affect SLOs? sounds like extra hop (Router) before fanout.

maya: Router is tiny — single RPC, colocated with API edge. Add a circuit-breaker. Overall expected added 1-3ms p50, but cache reductions should lower p95 significantly.

alex: agree to prototype. next: canary plan? I can own rollout.

maya: awesome. plan: feature-flag Router; start with read-only dashboards; 2% traffic canary -> 10% -> 50 -> 100; observe cache hit, p95, and incidents. Rollback if p95 increases >10%.

ci-bot: canary pipeline queued: ci/pipelines/access-router-proto (triggered by @alex)

pranav: implementation note: keep authz rules declarative (Rego) so Router can eval without pulling DB for each request.

sara: +1 on Rego. Also add audit logs for token issuance (org, user, rule-id).

maya: I'll open a tiny followup PR with interfaces and a draft rollout checklist. tagging @alex @pranav @sara for review :thumbsup:

alex: :thumbsup:

pranav: one more thought — fallback behavior: if Router unavailable, Broker should default to conservative deny or cached route? I'd prefer conservative deny to avoid data leaks.

julian: conservative deny will cause dashboard errors; maybe allow a short-lived cached token fallback for previously seen routes.

maya: agreed: fallback order: cached token (<=2m) -> deny. We'll document.

sara: sounds good. can we add a small e2e integration test that simulates policy bump and verifies invalidation?

maya: yes, will add. I'll post the PR URL in this thread when ready.
